title: Equipment suitability and inspection
audience: Trainee or new worker on the pressure cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Understand pressure, flow, reaction force, pressure ratings, hose compatibility and manufacturer-specified nozzles without prescribing unsafe settings.

instruction.heading: Pressure, flow and reaction force
instruction.body: Two quantities describe a pressure water system, and they are not the same thing. Pressure is the force the water is delivered at. Flow is the volume delivered in a given time. A cleaner's output depends on both, and the WorkSafe Victoria alert sorts high-pressure equipment by output, expressed in bar litres per minute, which combines the two. The alert places systems with an output of 800 to 5,600 bar litres per minute in Class A, and systems above 5,600 in Class B, which it describes as presenting a higher risk to the operator. A jet also pushes back on the equipment. That reaction force is why a lance is held firmly, why the operator's footing matters, and why a light or unsupported lance can move unexpectedly. This lesson does not set any working pressure or flow for a job. Those values come from the manufacturer's data for the equipment, and a worker who changes them to suit a surface is changing the equipment outside its design.

instruction.heading: Ratings, hoses and fittings
instruction.body: Every hose, fitting and part in the high-pressure path has a rating, and the rating must be at or above the maximum operating pressure of the equipment. The WorkSafe Victoria alert says hoses, fittings and parts should be the right size and compatible with each other, and rated at or above the equipment's maximum operating pressure. A hose that is rated for less than the machine can deliver is a failure waiting to happen. Check the rating printed on the hose and fitting against the equipment data before use, and do not mix hose brands or fitting types unless the manufacturer says they are compatible. The alert also says equipment and attachments must not be modified without written approval from the manufacturer or another competent person, and that repair and maintenance are for the manufacturer, its agent or a competent person. A modification the owner or worker makes on a site is a modification without approval.

instruction.heading: Nozzles and attachments
instruction.body: A nozzle sets the shape and the concentration of the jet, and so it changes the force on the surface and the risk to people in the area. Use only the nozzles the manufacturer specifies for the equipment. A nozzle that is worn, damaged, homemade or unidentified is not a suitable substitute, because its output is not known. Do not fit a nozzle found on site, or borrowed from another machine, until its specification has been confirmed against the manufacturer's data. Record the nozzle type and its source on the equipment record. The choice of nozzle must follow the scope and the surface test, not the wish to finish sooner.

instruction.heading: Inspection before use
instruction.body: Before the equipment is started, inspect it. Look at the hoses for cuts, abrasion, bulges and kinks, and at the fittings for leaks, cracks and worn threads. Check the trigger or control, the lance and its safety features, and the guards. Check the electrical lead and plug for damage, and test the RCD before use at the interval the guidance sets. The Queensland alert says a portable RCD should be tested daily or before each use, whichever is longer, and inspected every three months by a competent person. Do not run equipment with a damaged hose, a leaking fitting or an electrical fault. Tag it out, remove it from use and record the defect. A tag-out is not a repair. Only the manufacturer, its agent or a competent person can repair high-pressure equipment.

instruction.heading: Noise and hearing
instruction.body: Pressure equipment is often loud, and noise adds to the other hazards of the job. Safe Work Australia's exposure standard is that workers must not be exposed to noise above 85 decibels as an average over an eight-hour day. The page describes the duties to use control measures and provide personal protective equipment as separate duties, and it says that where a worker frequently wears hearing protection to stay below the standard, audiometric testing must be provided. The WorkSafe Victoria alert also calls for hearing protection where noise cannot be controlled. Choose the controls first, and use hearing protection where the controls do not reduce exposure enough.

instruction.heading: Training and competency
instruction.body: The WorkSafe Victoria alert says operators must be trained by a competent person, and that Class B operators must be trained and assessed through a registered training organisation. It also says trainers must be accredited, and that operators need refresher training at least every two years, and whenever new or more powerful equipment is introduced. This lesson is an introduction to equipment suitability and inspection. It does not give Class B competency, and it does not authorise work on equipment above the Class A range.

procedure: Identify the equipment make, model, serial number and its class from the manufacturer's data. Record the maximum operating pressure and output from the data sheet.
Check the rating on every hose, fitting and part against the equipment's maximum operating pressure, and reject any part rated lower.
Confirm that each nozzle is the manufacturer's specified type. Reject any unidentified or homemade nozzle until its specification is confirmed.
Complete the pre-use inspection of hoses, fittings, the trigger, the lance, the guards, the electrical lead and the plug.
Test the RCD at the interval the guidance sets, and record the test.
Tag out any equipment with a fault, remove it from use, and refer the repair to the manufacturer, its agent or a competent person.
Record the inspection, any nozzle or part change, and the hearing protection and noise controls chosen for the job.

workedExamples.situation: A hose on a machine has a rating lower than the machine's maximum operating pressure. The hose looks sound, and the job is a short one. This is an example job.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the machine be used with this hose?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The hose must be rated at or above the maximum operating pressure. A sound-looking hose with a lower rating is still outside its design. Tag the hose out, record the rating, and fit a hose rated at or above the maximum operating pressure from the manufacturer's data. Do not use the machine until the replacement is fitted and checked.

workedExamples.situation: A worker finds a lance nozzle in the back of the van with no label. It fits the lance, and it looks like the one used on the last job. This is an example job.
workedExamples.reasoning: Not until its specification is confirmed. An unidentified nozzle has an unknown output, and changing the nozzle changes the force of the jet. Leave it out of use, record it, and check the manufacturer's list for the equipment. Use a nozzle only where its type is named in the manufacturer's data for that machine.

workedExamples.situation: A job is booked as routine exterior cleaning, but the client asks for a stronger machine that is described as Class B. This is an example job.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you tell the client, and what do you do with the job?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop, and tell the client that Class B equipment is outside this course and requires training and assessment through a registered training organisation. Do not use or accept the machine on this basis. Refer the job, and record the request and the decision.

equipmentAndPpe: Manufacturer's manual and data sheet for each machine, with the class and maximum operating pressure recorded
Equipment register with make, model, serial number and nozzle type
Pre-use inspection checklist for hoses, fittings, trigger, lance, guards and electrical lead
RCD test device or the portable RCD's own test button, and a test log
Tags and a tag-out register for equipment removed from use
Eye protection and face shield for the operator, and hearing protection where noise cannot be controlled

commonErrors.error: Using a hose or fitting rated below the machine's maximum operating pressure.
commonErrors.prevention: Check every rating against the manufacturer's data before the machine is started.

commonErrors.error: Fitting a homemade, borrowed or unidentified nozzle.
commonErrors.prevention: Use only the nozzle type the manufacturer specifies, and confirm any other nozzle before use.

commonErrors.error: Skipping the pre-use inspection because the machine worked last time.
commonErrors.prevention: Complete the inspection before each use, and record it.

commonErrors.error: Modifying equipment or repairing it on site without approval.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer modifications and repairs to the manufacturer, its agent or a competent person.

commonErrors.error: Assuming pressure and flow can be changed to suit the surface.
commonErrors.prevention: Work within the manufacturer's data, and refer any need for a different setting.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Equipment class and training: the WorkSafe Victoria alert describes Class A and Class B by output, and requires Class B operators to be trained and assessed through a registered training organisation, with refresher training at least every two years. The alert cites AS/NZS 4233.1:2013 for the classes.
Modification and repair: the alert says equipment and attachments are not to be modified without written approval, and repairs are for the manufacturer, its agent or a competent person.
Electrical safety: the RCD test and inspection points come from the Queensland alert, which concerns inflatable balls, and are applied here by analogy.

Noise: the exposure standard is 85 decibels as an average over eight hours, with audiometric testing where protection is worn frequently above it. This lesson does not state a noise level for any particular machine. Read the manufacturer's data for that.
Completing this lesson does not give Class B competency, a high-pressure licence, or authority to repair or modify equipment.

qualityStandard: The equipment class and maximum operating pressure are identified from the manufacturer's data, and recorded.
Every hose, fitting and part is rated at or above the maximum operating pressure of the equipment.
Each nozzle is the manufacturer's specified type, or its specification is confirmed before use.
The pre-use inspection and the RCD test are completed and recorded before each use, and faulty equipment is tagged out.
documentationEvidence: Equipment register with make, model, serial number, class and maximum operating pressure from the manufacturer's data
Pre-use inspection log, with the RCD test record
Component rating record for hoses and fittings
Tag-out register with the date, the fault and the referral
Record of nozzle type and source for each job
summary: Pressure and flow both matter, and the manufacturer's data sets the working values for the equipment.
Every hose and fitting must be rated at or above the maximum operating pressure, and modifications need written approval.
Inspect the equipment before use, test the RCD, and tag out and refer any fault.
Class B equipment needs training and assessment through a registered training organisation, which this lesson does not give.

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the WorkSafe Victoria alert say about Class B equipment?
options: It covers systems with an output above 5,600 bar litres per minute
It covers home-use equipment with a garden hose and a trigger gun
It covers any equipment that has a hose and a trigger gun
It needs no training, because it is only a machine in the yard

knowledgeChecks.question: A hose is rated lower than the maximum operating pressure of the machine. What is correct?
options: Use it for a short job only, since the rating is close enough to the maximum for the work
Remove the rating label so the hose is not questioned on the job by anyone at all today
Tag the hose out and replace it with one rated at or above the maximum operating pressure
Add a clamp to the fitting and carry on with the job as planned for the day

knowledgeChecks.question: An unidentified nozzle is found on site. What is correct?
options: Fit it if it fits the lance and the hose connection on the machine today
Use it to get better results on the surface being cleaned at the site today
Do not use it until its specification is confirmed against the manufacturer's data
Test it on the owner's front windows before the main job starts on the day
